criteria.statement: The MCP server emits the CLI's own workflow YAML rather than a hand-built copy — byte-for-byte the output of renderWorkflowYaml, so the two cannot produce different files
criteria.test: packages/mcp/src/__tests__/phase5.test.ts::runProjectCreate > embeds the CLI's rendered workflow YAML verbatim

criteria.statement: Parity holds across inputs rather than for one fixed case — a different set of target branches still yields exactly what the CLI renders
criteria.test: packages/mcp/src/__tests__/phase5.test.ts::runProjectCreate > tracks the CLI's renderer when branches differ

criteria.statement: The four pieces the duplicate had dropped are present: the bot loop guard, the permissions block, contents: write, and commit-mode. Each caused a real failure — the guard stops the bot retriggering itself, permissions are required to push at all, and commit-mode is what readWorkflowCommitMode parses back to choose between a PR and a direct push
criteria.test: packages/mcp/src/__tests__/phase5.test.ts::runProjectCreate > carries the pieces the hand-built copy dropped

criteria.statement: The workflow path is a single exported constant. It was previously spelled out in seven places across the two packages — three times inside the CLI alone — and they disagreed, which is what allowed the filename split to exist at all

evidence.ref: WORKFLOW_RELATIVE_PATH is defined once in packages/cli/src/utils/workflow-path.ts and consumed by workflow-write.ts, workflow-read.ts, commands/init.ts, and the MCP's create-project.ts and phase5 tests. `grep -rn 'vocoder-translate.yml' packages/*/src --include=*.ts` outside tests now returns only the constant's own definition and one doc comment; `grep -rn 'vocoder\.yml'` returns only an explanatory comment describing the bug that was fixed.

criteria.statement: The tests assert against the CLI's exported constant and renderer rather than string literals, so a future change to either fails here instead of silently re-introducing a split

evidence.ref: phase5.test.ts previously asserted `.github/workflows/vocoder.yml` in three places — it was pinning the bug, and those three assertions failed the moment the fix landed, which is how the fix was confirmed to reach the output. They now import WORKFLOW_RELATIVE_PATH and renderWorkflowYaml from @vocoder/cli/lib. The package's vi.mock of that module uses importOriginal and overrides only VocoderAPI, so the real renderer and constant are exercised.

criteria.statement: No existing behaviour regressed across the SDK

evidence.ref: Full sdk suite green: core 112, react 246, extractor 98, plugin 14, cli 245, mcp 27 (up from 24). Gate reports Build, Typecheck, Lint, Unit and Disclosure passing; the only failure is the pre-existing constitution-copy drift described in the VOC-111 record, which CI skips because the sync script is unreachable when only this repo is checked out.

criteria.statement: This is the first slice of the ticket, not the whole of it — recorded so the remaining scope is a plan rather than an oversight

evidence.ref: Still outstanding on VOC-113: the headless runTranslate extraction (which is what makes vocoder_translate's hardcoded appDir '' impossible rather than merely fixed), writeApiKeyToEnv, writeVocoderConfig including apps[] for monorepos, writeLocaleFileTree, findOrphanedFiles, resolveLookupMatch, checkPlanLimits and getLimitErrorGuidance. Workflow generation was taken first because it was the single duplicate causing the most defects — four in one file.

criteria.statement: Per-app extraction lives in one implementation that both the CLI and the MCP server call. It previously existed twice, and the copies disagreed about the most consequential thing in the pipeline — which apps exist and what fingerprint scope each gets

evidence.ref: packages/cli/src/utils/extract-apps.ts exports extractApps and resolveAppDirs, both re-exported from @vocoder/cli/lib. commands/translate.ts calls them and keeps its spinner via the optional onAppStart/onAppDone callbacks — the only CLI-specific part left. mcp/src/tools/translate.ts calls the same two functions; its own extraction loop, include/exclude resolution and fingerprint computation are deleted.

criteria.statement: The MCP server no longer hardcodes a single root app. It previously passed appDir "" in the submission and computed the fingerprint scope as `${projectShortId}:`, so every monorepo submitted one merged string set under a scope the plugin never computes at build time

evidence.ref: grep for `appDir: ""` and for the root-only scope template in mcp/src/tools/translate.ts both return nothing. The submission now maps over the resolved apps, each carrying its own appDir, fingerprint and sourceEntriesHash.

criteria.statement: App-directory resolution is covered directly, including the precedence rules and the slash normalisation that keeps `--app-dir /apps/web/` and `apps/web` on the same fingerprint scope
criteria.test: packages/cli/src/__tests__/extract-apps.test.ts::resolveAppDirs > strips leading and trailing slashes from an explicit app dir

criteria.statement: Resolution never returns an empty list — root-level and monorepo projects stay on one code path because a project with no apps[] resolves to a single app whose directory is the empty string

The refactor was proven to sit on the real code path rather than beside it: the CLI's existing orchestrator tests failed when extraction was first imported from the wrong module, and passed once corrected

evidence.ref: extract-apps.ts initially imported StringExtractor from @vocoder/extractor rather than the CLI's own utils/extract.js re-export. Four tests in translate.test.ts failed immediately, because the suite mocks utils/extract.js and the new import bypassed that mock. utils/extract.ts is a pure re-export, so the two are identical at runtime and this was a testability defect rather than a production one — but it demonstrates the extracted code is genuinely what the orchestrator tests exercise. Corrected to import from ./extract.js; all 245 CLI tests pass.

criteria.statement: vocoder_regenerate_key selects the app matching the current checkout rather than whichever the lookup returned first. Taking existingApps[0] meant an agent working in apps/admin could rotate apps/web's API key — a silent, destructive mis-selection in any monorepo
criteria.test: packages/cli/src/__tests__/config-render.test.ts::resolveLookupMatch > prefers an exact appDir match over whatever came back first

criteria.statement: When no app matches and the repo has no whole-repo app, resolution returns null so the caller can name the missing directory, instead of silently proceeding with an unrelated app
criteria.test: packages/cli/src/__tests__/config-render.test.ts::resolveLookupMatch > returns null when nothing matches and there is no whole-repo app

criteria.statement: The generated vocoder.config no longer contains appId. It is not a field on VocoderConfig — TypeScript rejects it and the extractor's config parser drops it — so every agent following those instructions produced a file the user had to fix by hand
criteria.test: packages/cli/src/__tests__/config-render.test.ts::renderVocoderConfig > never emits appId — it is not a field on VocoderConfig

criteria.statement: No localesDir is pinned, so DEFAULT_LOCALES_DIR applies and a project laid out by an agent matches one laid out by `vocoder init`
criteria.test: packages/cli/src/__tests__/config-render.test.ts::renderVocoderConfig > never pins localesDir, so the SDK default applies

criteria.statement: Config generation follows the same render/write split as the workflow, so callers that hand text to someone else emit exactly what the CLI would have written

evidence.ref: renderVocoderConfig is extracted from writeVocoderConfig, which now delegates to it — mirroring renderWorkflowYaml / writeGitHubActionsWorkflow. Both are exported from @vocoder/cli/lib alongside resolveLookupMatch. `grep -c "appId: '"` in mcp/src/tools/regenerate-key.ts returns 0. Full sdk suite green at 790; cli 252 -> 260.
